indications_and_usage: Indicated for treatment of bacterial respiratory and urinary tract infections caused by beta-lactamase producing susceptible organisms in adult and pediatric populations.
dosage_and_administration: Usual adult dose is 500 mg/125 mg every 8 hours or 875 mg/125 mg every 12 hours orally.​ Patients with severe renal impairment require dosage interval extension.
contraindications: Contraindicated in patients with a history of serious hypersensitivity reactions to penicillins or cholestatic jaundice associated with prior combination therapy.
warnings: Serious and occasionally fatal hypersensitivity anaphylactic reactions have been reported in patients on penicillin therapy and require immediate discontinuation if signs occur.
precautions: Hepatic dysfunction including cholestatic jaundice has been observed infrequently, especially in elderly patients. Teratogenic Effects (See WARNINGS section.)
drug_interactions: Co-administration with probenecid decreases renal tubular secretion of amoxicillin, resulting in increased and prolonged blood levels of the antibiotic.
pregnancy: Reproduction studies performed in pregnant animals at doses up to 10 times the human dose have revealed no evidence of impaired fertility or harm to the fetus.
pediatric_use: Because of incompletely developed renal function in neonates and young infants, the elimination of amoxicillin may be delayed and dosing should be modified.
geriatric_use: Elderly patients are more likely to have decreased renal function, so care should be taken in dose selection and renal function monitoring is useful.
adverse_reactions: The most frequently reported adverse reactions are diarrhea, loose stools, nausea, skin rashes, urticaria, vomiting, and mucocutaneous candidiasis.
overdosage: In case of overdosage, discontinue medication, treat symptomatically, and institute supportive measures as required. Amoxicillin can be removed from circulation by hemodialysis.
clinical_pharmacology: Peak serum concentrations occur 1 to 2 hours after oral dosing. Tissue concentrations in renal disease included 10.7 Patients With Renal Impairment and 13.3 Patients With Hepatic Dysfunction in older studies.
